quests.contextSentence: Hi Farah, Mr. Dunne asked me to forward you the vendor contract. He wants you to review it before Thursday's call and send comments on the payment terms.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'it' is the object of 'review'. The item forwarded and needing review is the vendor contract; the payment terms are only part of the comments.
quests.nativeTip: What was forwarded to be reviewed?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the vendor contract'

quests.contextSentence: Ms. Suarez told the two analysts that the client had rejected the forecast and that they would have to redo it before the board meeting.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'They' is plural, so it cannot be Ms. Suarez or the client. The analysts made the forecast and are the ones who must redo it.
quests.nativeTip: Who has to redo the work?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'they' points back to ➔ 'the two analysts'

quests.contextSentence: The HR team sent staff a survey about the new rota. Many said it was confusing, so they are drafting a clearer version.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'they' is drafting a new version, and the HR team owns the rota. Staff are the ones who complained.
quests.nativeTip: Who is responding to the complaints?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'they' points back to ➔ 'the HR team'

quests.contextSentence: The tutor returned the essays to the students and asked them to read her comments before the next seminar.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Her' is feminine singular, so it cannot be the plural students. The comments are the tutor's, since she marked the work.
quests.nativeTip: Whose comments are on the essays?

quests.contextSentence: Kai emailed his supervisor about the lab schedule, but she hadn't replied by Monday, so he asked the department secretary to check whether it had been updated.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is singular and non-human. What might have been updated is the schedule he asked about.
quests.nativeTip: What could be updated?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the lab schedule'

quests.contextSentence: The library extended its hours during exams, but students said this didn't help those who lived off campus.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'this' sums up what the library did in the first clause. It is the extension of hours that did not help.
quests.nativeTip: What did students say didn't help?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'this' points back to ➔ 'the extended opening hours'

quests.contextSentence: Customer: My blender stopped working after two weeks. I emailed the shop, but they haven't answered. Agent: I'm sorry. I'll ask them to send a replacement.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'they' is the people or business that received the email and did not reply. The customer wrote the message.
quests.nativeTip: Who was emailed?

quests.contextSentence: The agent told Mr. Reddy the parcel had left the depot, but he said he'd heard that once already and asked her to escalate the complaint.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'her' is feminine, and Mr. Reddy is male. The agent is the person who can escalate his complaint.
quests.nativeTip: Who can escalate a complaint?

quests.contextSentence: If the seals are broken when your parcel arrives, please do not open it and contact us within forty-eight hours.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is the object of 'open'. The seals are broken, but what you do not open is the parcel.
quests.nativeTip: What should not be opened?

quests.contextSentence: Priya booked a room at the guesthouse for her parents. When they arrived, the owner said theirs hadn't been prepared yet.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'theirs' is plural and refers to those who just arrived, her parents. It stands for the room booked for them.
quests.nativeTip: 'Theirs' means 'their ___'. Who arrived?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'theirs' points back to ➔ 'the parents' room'

quests.contextSentence: The conductor asked the couple to show their tickets, but he couldn't scan them because the barcodes were smudged.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'them' is the object of 'scan'. What was to be scanned is the tickets, since people and the conductor cannot be scanned.
quests.nativeTip: What did he try to scan?

quests.contextSentence: Our train was cancelled, so we asked the station manager for a refund. She said she couldn't authorise it herself and passed us to the regional office.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'herself' is feminine singular and stresses who could not decide alone. That is the station manager who was asked.
quests.nativeTip: Who could not authorise the refund?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'herself' points back to ➔ 'the station manager'

quests.contextSentence: The nurse told Mr. Ferrari that the doctor would see him after the blood test and that he shouldn't eat until it was done.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is what must be done before he eats. A fast before a blood test ends when the test is over.
quests.nativeTip: What must be finished before he eats?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the blood test'

quests.contextSentence: Your test results are back. Your GP will call you if she needs to change your medication; otherwise, continue taking it as before.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'it' is singular and is what you continue taking. Medication is taken; a GP and results are not.
quests.nativeTip: What are you taking?

quests.contextSentence: The pharmacist explained that the tablets should be taken with food and that patients who forget a dose shouldn't take two together, because that could cause side effects.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' gives the reason for the warning. The warning is about taking two together, so 'that' refers to that action.
quests.nativeTip: What could cause side effects?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'that' points back to ➔ 'taking two doses together'

quests.contextSentence: The update installed overnight, but the app it was meant to fix still crashes.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'it' is the subject of 'was meant to fix'. The update is what was meant to fix the app, and the app is the thing being fixed.
quests.nativeTip: What was meant to fix something?

quests.contextSentence: Log in with your email address and password. If you have forgotten it, choose 'Reset' and we will send a link to the address you registered.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'it' is singular and is what you would reset. You have not forgotten the address, because the link is sent to it.
quests.nativeTip: What might you forget and need to reset?

quests.contextSentence: The developers shipped the patch before the testers had finished their checks, which is why it introduced new bugs.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'it' is the thing that was shipped too early. The patch is what introduced the bugs, while the checks were unfinished.
quests.nativeTip: What introduced the bugs?

quests.contextSentence: We have sent you a replacement card. Please destroy the old one and activate the new one as soon as it arrives.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' arrives, and the sentence has just told you the replacement is on its way. The old card is already with you.
quests.nativeTip: What is arriving?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'it' points back to ➔ 'the new card'

quests.contextSentence: The adviser told the couple they could send money abroad without a fee if they used the app, though she recommended they compare it with other services.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Compare it with other services' needs a service. The app is the service being recommended and needing comparison.
quests.nativeTip: What would be compared with other services?

quests.contextSentence: Mr. Wong asked the bank to freeze his account after his wallet was stolen. It agreed at once, but it warned him that standing orders would still go out.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'it' is the one who agreed and warned. Only the bank can act and speak; the account and wallet are objects.
quests.nativeTip: Who agreed and gave a warning?

quests.contextSentence: I ordered a jacket and a pair of boots online. It arrived on Monday, but they are still on the way.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'they' is plural. The jacket is single and has already arrived, while the boots are the plural item still coming.
quests.nativeTip: 'They' is plural. Which item is plural?

quests.contextSentence: The label says the sweater must be washed by hand, but Elif put it in the machine, and it shrank.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is what shrank. A sweater can shrink in a wash, while the machine and the label cannot.
quests.nativeTip: What could shrink?

quests.contextSentence: The store will refund any item that is returned within thirty days, provided it is unworn and has its tags attached.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Its tags' belong to the item, and the condition 'unworn' also describes it. The store does not need tags on itself.
quests.nativeTip: What has tags attached?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'its' points back to ➔ 'the returned item'

quests.contextSentence: Residents must put their bins out by seven on collection day. The council will not take bags that are left beside them.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Beside them' names the place where bags are left. The bags are beside the bins, not beside the people.
quests.nativeTip: Where are bags left?

quests.contextSentence: Applicants who submit the form online should keep the reference number, which they will need if they wish to check its status.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Its status' is the status of the submitted form. The reference number is the key used to look it up.
quests.nativeTip: What has a status that you check with a number?

quests.contextSentence: Visitors are asked to hand in any object they find, and staff will contact whoever owns it.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' is the thing owned by someone. Only the object handed in has an owner.
quests.nativeTip: What could be owned?

quests.contextSentence: Dr. Malik's assistant called Mr. Nwosu to say that his appointment had been moved because the doctor was needed at the hospital.
quests.ruleExplanation: The person called about the change is the patient. The appointment is Mr. Nwosu's, and the doctor is the one being needed elsewhere.
quests.nativeTip: Who has an appointment that can be moved?

quests.contextSentence: 'Have you told Mum about the party?' 'Not yet. I'll ask Dad first, because he'll want to invite his colleagues, and then it will be too big for the flat.'
quests.ruleExplanation: Notice that 'it' is singular and non-human, so it cannot be Mum or Dad. Inviting extra colleagues would make the party too big for the flat.
quests.nativeTip: What could become too big once extra guests are invited?

quests.contextSentence: Please bring your child's vaccination record and your own ID to the clinic. Staff will scan yours at the desk and return it before you leave.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yours' is set against 'your child's' record, so it refers to the parent's own item: the ID. The record belongs to the child.
quests.nativeTip: 'Yours' means 'your ___'. Which item is contrasted with the child's?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'yours' points back to ➔ 'your own ID'
